transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you for seeing me. I, um... well, I hope I'm not wasting your time, honestly. It's probably nothing major, just... my wife suggested I come in. I guess what finally made me agree is that I just... I don't know, I don't really care about the things that used to keep me balanced anymore. 

Like, I used to love sailing races, and I had my Saturday shift at the historical society, which I always looked forward to. Even tinkering out in the woodshop... but lately, they all just feel like chores, you know? I just keep putting them off. I'm sure it's just a phase, right? I mean, everyone gets in a rut sometimes... is that something people come here for?
Have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, lately?

Oh, um, no, I wouldn't say depressed. I hope I didn't give you the wrong impression just now. I mean, I get up, I go to work—I manage projects, so I have to stay pretty on top of things, and I'm still doing all of that just fine. I'm definitely not sitting around feeling sad or crying or anything like that. 

It's really just that... flatness with my hobbies that I mentioned. But during the day, I feel fine, mostly. Just normal, I suppose. Does that make sense? I really don't want to overstate things if it's just a normal slump.

Have you noticed that things you used to enjoy, like time with friends or family, or even small daily pleasures like a good meal or a favorite TV show, don’t seem to give you the same satisfaction they used to?

Well, um... I guess maybe a little bit? I really don't want to sound ungrateful, because I have a great family and I'm proud of my work. But, yeah... like, my wife and kids can be joking around and laughing at dinner, or I can finally finish a really difficult project milestone at the office. And I know those things should feel good. I know I should be happy and celebrating in those moments. 

But mostly, I just feel... I don't know, kind of flat? Just a little removed from it all, if that makes sense. I hope that doesn't make me sound terrible or cold. I'm sure everyone gets a little detached when they're busy, right? Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you noticed that you no longer get the same enjoyment out of things that used to make you happy, like spending time with your family, finishing a good book, or even just relaxing after work?

Um, well, I think that's sort of what I was just trying to explain... I hope I didn't confuse things just now. 

I mean, I still relax after work just fine, and I read quite a bit—mostly history books—and I still like finishing them. It's not that I get zero enjoyment out of my day-to-day life, I promise. It's really just that... that slight detached feeling I was just talking about with my hobbies and sometimes at dinner. But I haven't noticed it taking over everything else, like reading or just winding down. 

I wouldn't say I've lost all my happiness or anything dramatic like that. I hope I'm giving you the right information here... am I explaining it okay? I just really don't want to make it sound worse than it actually is.
Can you think of a time recently when you genuinely felt happy or excited about something, even for a short moment?

Um, well... I'm trying to think. I know I brought up dinner with my wife and kids a minute ago, and finishing those big project milestones at work. And, well, to answer your question... I guess I really can't think of a time I felt genuinely excited lately, even in those moments. 

Like I said earlier, I know I *should* feel it, and I really want to—I don't want you to think I don't care about my family or my job, because I do. But it just stays... flat. Even when they're all laughing and having a great time, I just feel a little removed from it. 

I hope I'm not sounding like a broken record, repeating myself like that. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answer. Is that the kind of example you were looking for?
Can you describe how you feel when you finish a good book or complete a project at work—do those accomplishments still feel satisfying, or do they seem to lack the sense of reward they used to have?

Um, well... I know we keep circling back to this, and I really hope I'm not being difficult or repeating myself too much. I want to make sure I'm answering you right. 

With the books, like I mentioned, I still enjoy finishing those. That still feels pretty good. But with the work projects... well, it's like I was saying before about dinner with my wife and kids. When they're all laughing, or when I hit that big milestone at the office, I know I *should* feel really satisfied and happy about it. But I just... I don't know, I just feel a bit flat. Kind of removed from the reward of it, I guess? 

It's not that I don't care, I promise. I just don't get that same spark I used to. I hope that makes sense? I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining about my life, because I know I have it good. Am I explaining that okay?
Can you tell me if you’ve noticed a change in how you feel about your accomplishments, like whether finishing a big project at work feels as rewarding as it used to?

Oh, um... I'm so sorry, did I not explain that very well just a second ago? I feel terrible if I'm being confusing and making you repeat yourself. 

But, um, yes, like I was just trying to say... finishing a big project just doesn't feel quite as rewarding as it used to. It's just that same flat feeling I mentioned. I really don't want you to think I'm slacking off at the office or anything, because I still do a good job and get everything done on time. It's just the personal satisfaction part that's changed a little bit. 

I really hope I'm answering this right for you... did you need me to give a different kind of example? I want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need.
Can you tell me if you’ve lost interest in activities that you used to find meaningful or enjoyable, even things that were once important to you, like your hobbies or spending time with loved ones?

Well, um... yeah. That's actually... honestly, that's kind of what finally made me agree to come in and see you. I hate admitting it, because I've always prided myself on staying active and involved. I really don't want you to think I'm just sitting around being lazy. 

But... I just really don't seem to care about the things that used to keep me balanced anymore. Like the sailing races I usually do, or my Saturday shift at the historical society... even just tinkering out in my woodshop. Lately, they all just feel like chores that I keep finding excuses to put off. 

I feel awful saying that out loud, because people count on me for some of those things, and I know I should want to do them. I just... I hope that's the kind of information you need? Is it normal to feel that way, or am I making things more complicated?
Have you been feeling emotionally detached or numb, even when you're with people you care about or in situations that used to make you feel connected?

Oh, um... I know I touched on this a little bit earlier, and I'm so sorry if I keep bringing up the same things. I hope it's okay if I use that same example again, I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answer. 

But yes, like I was saying about dinner time... my wife and kids can be sitting right there, laughing and having a great time, and I know I should feel really good and connected to them in that moment. But mostly, I just feel... flat. Just a little removed from it all, kind of like with those difficult project milestones at work I mentioned. 

I really, really don't want to sound like a cold person, or like I don't love my family, because I absolutely do. They're everything to me. It's just that the feeling inside isn't quite matching up with what's happening around me right now. Am I making sense? I can try to think of a different example if that would be more helpful for your notes.
Can you tell me how long you've been feeling this way—this flatness and lack of enjoyment in things you used to care about?

Well, um... I guess it's been a while now. I really hope I'm not making it sound like I've just been ignoring a problem for ages, because I've really been trying to push through it and stay productive. 

But, um... it started right around the time of that scaffold accident we had during the business readjustment phase. So... I guess that makes it a little over a year now? 

I know I probably should have said something sooner, and I feel terrible taking up your time with something that's been going on for that long. I just kept thinking I could snap out of it on my own, you know? I really hope I didn't wait too long to come in... is it okay that it's been a year?
Over the past year, have there been periods lasting at least two weeks where you felt this flatness or lack of enjoyment most of the time, nearly every day, not just occasionally?

Oh, um... I want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture here. I really wouldn't say it's been... constant like that. Not for two whole weeks straight, every single day. 

I really try my best to keep a good attitude and, you know, push through for my family and my team at work. So I definitely still have plenty of good days where I'm engaged and functioning just fine. It's more... it just kind of comes and goes, I guess? 

I hope I'm not confusing things or messing up your evaluation by saying that. I just definitely don't want to make it sound worse than it actually is, or make you think I'm just letting myself go completely. Is... is that helpful? I hope that's an okay answer.
In the past year, was there ever a time when you felt this way—flat or not getting enjoyment out of things—for at least two weeks straight, without much relief?

Um, no... I don't think so. I really don't think there's ever been a time where it was just... two weeks of nothing but that flat feeling. 

I mean, I'm so sorry if I'm repeating myself, I just want to make sure I'm not giving you the wrong idea. Like I said, I really do try to stay on top of things. I wouldn't let myself just check out for two whole weeks without pulling it together, you know? I really do have good days mixed in there, where I'm completely fine and enjoying things just like normal. 

I hope that's the right kind of answer? I just don't want you to think I'm, you know, completely falling apart or not trying my best.
Have you ever had a period in your life before this past year when you felt down or lost interest in things for more than two weeks at a time?

No, never. I mean, I've always been a pretty upbeat guy, you know? I really pride myself on being dependable and keeping a positive attitude, especially at work and for my family. 

I don't think I've ever had a time where I just... let myself go like that for two whole weeks. I'd hate to think I was ever that checked out. I've always been able to just roll up my sleeves and push through whatever stress was going on. 

I hope that makes sense? I just want to be sure I'm giving you what you need for this. I promise I'm not trying to hide anything, I've just always been pretty good at bouncing back before all this scaffold stuff happened. Is that... does that help?

Can you think back over the past year and tell me if there was ever a time when you felt this flatness or lack of enjoyment for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks in a row, even if it was just once?

Um, I'm really sorry, I feel like I might be frustrating you since we keep coming back to this. I must not be explaining myself very well, and I apologize for that. I promise I'm really searching my memory here to make sure I'm giving you the right information. 

But... no, even just looking for one time in the past year, it's never been two full weeks of just feeling flat every single day. I always manage to pull my weight on my projects at work and be there for my family, so there are always good days mixed in. I'd never let it get that bad for that long without doing something about it, you know? 

I hope it's okay that I keep saying no to this one. I'm really not trying to be difficult or ruin your evaluation, I just want to give you the most accurate answer. Am I... am I doing this right? I really want to make sure I'm being helpful.

Um, I... I know you're asking again, and I'm so sorry if I'm not giving you the answer you're looking for. I really don't want to be a difficult patient. I just...

Oh, wow, you really remembered my hobbies. I appreciate you taking the time to note those down. But, um... gosh, I feel terrible because I know we keep circling back to this, and I really, really don't want to seem like I'm stonewalling you or being uncooperative. I promise I'm giving it a lot of thought. 

But... no. Even with the woodshop or the historical society stuff... I always keep up with them. I mean, sure, maybe I'll miss a weekend if a big project at work is running behind, but never two weeks straight where I just completely lose interest or stop caring. I always make a point to stay engaged. I feel like if I just dropped my commitments, I'd be letting people down, and I really pride myself on being someone people can count on. 

I hope that's the kind of detail you're looking for? I'm so sorry if I'm making your job harder by not having a 'yes' for you here. I just want to make absolutely sure I'm giving you the honest truth so I don't mess up your evaluation. Am I doing okay?
